section_summary: This section consists chiefly of inquiries from holders of defaulted Japanese government, municipal, and utility bonds, with State Department replies explaining its policy and requesting details of holdings and citizenship. It also includes correspondence about British bondholders, the distinction between bonds and equity interests in Japan’s monopoly dissolution program, and efforts to pass bond information to U.S. representatives in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Reply to Alice McGhee about her Japanese government bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains trading restrictions and its policy on defaulted Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss refers McGhee to her banker and the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, requests details of her bond and citizenship, and says any government action will be announced publicly.

subfiles.title: Alice McGhee’s inquiry about a Japanese Imperial bond
subfiles.about: McGhee asks whether her Japanese Imperial bond has a market and what she should do with it.
subfiles.summary: Asks for advice about selling or disposing of her bond.

subfiles.title: Reply to Colonel Irving A. Lindberg
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Lindberg’s inquiry about his Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Luthringer describes foreign bond investment as a private risk, suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and says the peace settlement and priority of war claims remain uncertain.

subfiles.title: Japanese bonds held by Colonel Lindberg
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards Lindberg’s description of his 1924 Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Lindberg reports owning $6,000 face value and supplies terms of the 1924 issue.

subfiles.title: Instruction to deliver Lindberg reply
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Managua
subfiles.about: The Department sends its reply to Lindberg for delivery.
subfiles.summary: Requests delivery of the enclosed bondholder letter unless the mission objects.

subfiles.title: Frederick C. Slee’s bondholding details
subfiles.about: Slee reports Treasury filings and his Japanese bond holdings.
subfiles.summary: He lists $5,000 in 1954 bonds and $8,000 in 1965 bonds, with unpaid coupons attached.

subfiles.title: Reply to Frederick C. Slee
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Slee’s bond information and explains its policy.
subfiles.summary: Corliss records the information, refers Slee to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and notes uncertainty about peace settlement provisions and war claims.

subfiles.title: File note on an unanswered letter
subfiles.about: A lost file caused a reply to be abandoned.
subfiles.summary: The file was found too late for a reply to be sent.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Canby correspondence
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Bern
subfiles.about: The Department asks the legation to forward its reply to Edmund Canby.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Canby’s letter and a proposed response for forwarding if there is no objection.

subfiles.title: Copy of Edmund Canby’s inquiry
subfiles.about: Canby urges protection of holders of the 1907 Japanese sterling loan.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether assets found in Tokyo can pay principal and interest owed to investors.

subfiles.title: Reply to Edmund Canby
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department directs Canby to the London Corporation of Foreign Bondholders.
subfiles.summary: Corliss explains that the corporation represents holders of sterling bonds, including holders outside Britain.

subfiles.title: Edmund Canby’s original inquiry
subfiles.about: Canby seeks action for investors in the 1907 Japanese Imperial loan.
subfiles.summary: He argues that Allied control of Japanese assets should permit payment of the loan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding a Japanese bonds letter
subfiles.about: De Wolf forwards a letter about Japanese bonds discussed by telephone.
subfiles.summary: Attaches the bond letter for Whitman.

subfiles.title: Memorandum routing a bond payment request
subfiles.about: Shaskan routes a request concerning payment of Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the bond inquiry for Corliss’s attention.

subfiles.title: Guaranty Trust inquiry about Tokyo and Toho bonds
subfiles.from: Arthur F. Burke, Guaranty Trust Company of New York
subfiles.about: Burke requests information about utility bond indentures and Mitsui Bank’s trusteeship.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether required company statements are reaching the trustee, mortgage terms are being observed, and Japanese security holders receive payments despite defaults on dollar bonds.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Arthur F. Burke
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Krentz, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department reports that it has sent Burke’s inquiry to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Krentz promises to communicate again after the Political Adviser reports.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate utility bond interests
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Burke’s letter and requests an investigation.
subfiles.summary: Asks the Political Adviser to obtain the information Burke seeks about American bondholders’ interests.

subfiles.title: London airgram about publishing bondholder information
subfiles.about: The embassy asks whether a correspondent may share its bondholder letter with The Financial Times.
subfiles.summary: The proposed publication concerns British holders of prewar Japanese bonds and interest arrears.

subfiles.title: Permission to share London embassy letter
subfiles.about: The Department approves publication after correcting language about Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: It permits sharing the letter with The Financial Times and replaces the technically inaccurate word “vested.”

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Julia L. Shine
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges details of Shine’s Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: Her information will be placed in departmental files.

subfiles.title: Julia L. Shine’s bond details
subfiles.about: Shine provides purchase, citizenship, and interest payment details for her bond.
subfiles.summary: She bought a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light bond in 1928; its last interest payment was in June 1941.

subfiles.title: Ralph Wierenga’s bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Wierenga seeks information about $4,000 in Japanese external bonds.
subfiles.summary: He asks what can be learned about his Japanese External 6½ percent bonds; page 234 repeats the inquiry in a partial copy.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ralph Wierenga
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department requests purchase and citizenship details and explains its bondholder policy.
subfiles.summary: Corliss offers to record Wierenga’s holdings, refers him to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and notes that peace settlement provisions remain unknown.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Wierenga’s details
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges additional information about Wierenga’s bonds.
subfiles.summary: His information will be added to the Department’s record.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Wierenga inquiry
subfiles.about: Treasury sends Wierenga’s inquiry to State for consideration and reply.
subfiles.summary: Encloses his letter and Treasury’s acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to Wierenga
subfiles.about: Treasury acknowledges Wierenga’s inquiry about Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Advises that the inquiry has been referred to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Wierenga’s purchase details
subfiles.about: Wierenga lists dates, prices, and bond numbers for his $4,000 holding.
subfiles.summary: He reports four purchases of Japanese External 6½ percent dollar bonds between 1933 and 1937.

subfiles.title: Paul W. Fent’s Tokyo Electric Light inquiry
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Fent asks whether overdue interest on his Tokyo Electric Light bond can be collected.
subfiles.summary: He describes a $1,000 bond and unpaid coupons from December 1941 through June 1946.

subfiles.title: File note on Fent’s unanswered inquiry
subfiles.about: A lost file caused Fent’s inquiry to go unanswered.
subfiles.summary: The file was found too late for a reply.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning the Stenger estate bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department distinguishes Japanese bonds from equity interests and explains its policy.
subfiles.summary: Corliss says an August press release concerned equity, not government bonds. He offers to record estate holdings, requests acquisition and citizenship details, and refers Reck to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Reck’s inquiry for the Stenger estate
subfiles.about: Reck lists Japanese and German bonds held by Frank M. Stenger’s estate.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether the estate must file statements under the recently reported Japanese securities program.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ruth S. Reed
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds about Tokyo Electric Light bonds held by Reed and her stepfather.
subfiles.summary: Corliss explains that the August press release concerned equity interests, offers to record bond details and citizenship, and points to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Ruth S. Reed’s bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Reed asks about registering Tokyo Electric Light bonds held by her and John P. Whaley.
subfiles.summary: She supplies bond numbers and purchase information after reading a press notice seeking information on Japanese securities.

subfiles.title: Urgent routing note on bond inquiry
subfiles.about: A bond inquiry is routed to Corliss for a rapid reply.
subfiles.summary: The note says the matter is to be answered within 24 hours.

subfiles.title: Congressional liaison memorandum
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: A congressional letter about a Japanese municipal bond is referred to the division.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Representative Izac’s letter for handling.

subfiles.title: Representative Izac’s municipal bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Izac requests advice for an attorney whose client possesses a Japanese municipal bond.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether the bond has value and what disposition is possible, enclosing the attorney’s letter.

subfiles.title: Oswald C. Ludwig’s letter about a found bond
subfiles.about: Ludwig seeks advice about ownership and handling of a bearer municipal bond found in San Diego County.
subfiles.summary: He describes unpaid coupons and asks how wartime circumstances affect the finder’s rights.

subfiles.title: Halsey, Stuart inquiry about bond registration
subfiles.from: V. Savage, Halsey, Stuart and Company
subfiles.about: Savage asks whether Japanese bond registration is compulsory and whether forms exist.
subfiles.summary: Also requests information about planned departmental action concerning the securities.

subfiles.title: Reply to Stewart C. Pratt on Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its approach to defaulted, government-guaranteed Ujigawa Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss says State has supplied Japanese governmental dollar bond information to its Political Adviser in Tokyo and will forward Pratt’s letter. He requests holder and citizenship details, refers holders to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and says no further individual measures appear useful yet.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding National City Bank letter
subfiles.about: The Department sends Pratt’s Ujigawa bond letter for use in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the bank’s account to the Political Adviser and relevant Allied staff.

subfiles.title: National City Bank account of Ujigawa bonds
subfiles.from: Stewart C. Pratt, National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: The bank documents the Ujigawa bond mortgage and Japanese government guarantee.
subfiles.summary: Pratt describes the 1925 issue, its factory estate security, and a 1939 transfer of some property. He reproduces a Japanese government guarantee of principal and interest and asks that Allied authorities protect bondholders.

subfiles.title: Erlus McConnell’s appeal about Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: McConnell asks about redeeming Japanese bonds bought with savings.
subfiles.summary: He argues that Japanese assets should help pay American holders and worries that British holders may fare better.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to McConnell
subfiles.about: Treasury acknowledges McConnell’s bond inquiry and refers it to State.
subfiles.summary: Advises that State handles inquiries about foreign debt.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of McConnell’s letter
subfiles.about: Treasury forwards McConnell’s request for information about Japanese bond redemption.
subfiles.summary: Encloses his letter and Treasury’s acknowledgment for State’s reply.

subfiles.title: Reply to V. Savage about securities registration
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department clarifies its Japanese securities notice and policies for different holdings.
subfiles.summary: Registration was voluntary, used no special forms, and primarily concerned equity interests affected by monopoly dissolution. Corliss discusses private bonds, government-guaranteed bonds, direct communication with Japan, and information holders may submit.

subfiles.title: Savage’s follow-up on bond registration
subfiles.from: V. Savage, Halsey, Stuart and Company
subfiles.about: Savage repeats questions after receiving no answer to an August letter.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether registration is compulsory, whether forms are needed, and what action State plans.

subfiles.title: Reply about Saxton holdings
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to a report of Tokyo Electric Light bonds held for British clients.
subfiles.summary: Corliss says the monopoly dissolution notice addressed American equity holders, and suggests the bank contact the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council about the bonds.

subfiles.title: Bank of Montreal report for the Saxtons
subfiles.about: The bank reports a $5,000 Tokyo Electric Light holding for Clifford and Gwendolen Saxton.
subfiles.summary: It submits the information in response to notices about protecting interests during monopoly dissolution.

subfiles.title: Reply about Gertrude P. Race’s bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to a report of a Tokyo Electric Light bond held for a British client.
subfiles.summary: Corliss explains that the equity notice did not cover the bond and directs the bank toward the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Bank of Montreal report for Gertrude P. Race
subfiles.about: The bank reports a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light bond held for Race.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the holding in connection with the Allied monopoly dissolution program.

subfiles.title: Mark Mayfield’s inquiry about registration
subfiles.to: Office of the Japanese Embassy, Washington
subfiles.about: Mayfield asks whether he must register Japanese government and Taiwan Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: He lists bond numbers and requests instructions to safeguard his interests.

subfiles.title: Cover letter resending Mayfield reply
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department resends an earlier reply returned as undeliverable.
subfiles.summary: Encloses its March 18 response at Mayfield’s Carlinville address.

subfiles.title: Original reply to Mark Mayfield
subfiles.about: The Department explains its policy on Mayfield’s government and government-guaranteed bonds.
subfiles.summary: It describes the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and information supplied to Tokyo, requests acquisition and citizenship details, and says future holder action will be announced.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Byrd about Carbaugh’s bond
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses Flora Carbaugh’s City of Tokyo bond.
subfiles.summary: Marshall describes the bondholder policy, the Council’s work, and uncertainty over peace settlement terms. He invites purchase details and returns Reverend Carbaugh’s letter.

subfiles.title: Copy of Reverend Carbaugh’s bond description
subfiles.about: Carbaugh identifies his mother’s 1927 City of Tokyo gold bond.
subfiles.summary: He supplies the bond number, rate, maturity, payment location, and his mother’s name.

subfiles.title: Senator Byrd’s referral of Carbaugh inquiry
subfiles.about: Byrd sends Carbaugh’s inquiry to the Department for comment.
subfiles.summary: Requests an assessment and return of the enclosed letter.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Kichitaro Mutow’s utility bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses Mutow’s Japanese utility bonds and possible claims.
subfiles.summary: Corliss explains policy for private and government-guaranteed obligations, cites information sent to Tokyo, and offers to record Mutow’s holdings if he is an American citizen and supplies purchase and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Stanton’s inquiry for Kichitaro Mutow
subfiles.about: Stanton asks how Mutow can protect or recover his Japanese utility bond investments.
subfiles.summary: He recounts Mutow’s purchases, wartime evacuation, and concerns about utility nationalization and property transfers, enclosing a list of holdings.

subfiles.title: Schedule of Kichitaro Mutow’s bond holdings
subfiles.from: Louis B. Stanton, for Kichitaro Mutow
subfiles.about: The enclosure lists Mutow’s Japanese utility bonds and unpaid coupon periods.
subfiles.summary: It itemizes Tokyo Electric Light, Oriental Development, Great Consolidated Electric Power, and Shingetsu Electric Power bonds, including bond numbers and payment agents. It notes Treasury licensing blocked payment of some coupons held by Guaranty Trust.
